version: AgentCore harness GA (docs 2026-10-15); SDKs bedrock-agentcore 1.18.1+, starter toolkit 0.3.14+

facts.claim: Default tools shell and file_operations are available in every session unless restricted with allowedTools; if allowedTools is omitted all tools are allowed.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: allowedTools scopes LLM tool selection only; InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand executes commands without the LLM and needs its own IAM action.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: AgentCore Policy intercepts all Gateway traffic and evaluates it against Cedar (or Dogwood) policies before tool access; supports session-aware temporal conditions.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D01.rationale: Harness: all tools incl. shell and file_operations are allowed unless allowedTools is set; human-in-the-loop via inline_function tools; deterministic Cedar/Dogwood policies on Gateway tool calls (default stance not stated in pages read).

facts.claim: Every harness session runs in its own Firecracker microVM in AgentCore Runtime; no shared state or filesystem.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: BeyondTrust Phantom Labs (Mar 2026) reported Code Interpreter sandbox mode still permits DNS lookups usable as a covert channel; AWS response reported inconsistently (documentation/VPC-mode guidance); no CVE.
facts.label: third-party-report

D02.rationale: Each harness session runs in its own Firecracker microVM; Code Interpreter/Browser are separate sandboxes. Code Interpreter 'sandbox' network mode was reported (BeyondTrust, Mar 2026) to permit DNS egress.

facts.claim: 'By default, harness sessions run on the public network. To access private resources ... deploy the harness in your VPC.'
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: CSA research note recommends VPC mode with Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall for Code Interpreter.
facts.label: third-party-report

D03.rationale: Harness sessions run on the public network by default; VPC mode is opt-in; DNS firewall controls only available in VPC mode.

facts.claim: remote_mcp tool config supports plaintext headers or ${arn:...} references to Token Vault API-key credential providers; docs advise Gateway + Identity for managed rotation and OAuth.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: Registry: centralized catalog with governed publish/review/approve workflow for agents, MCP servers, tools and skills.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D05.rationale: Gateway converts APIs/Lambda to MCP tools with inbound/outbound auth and Policy; Registry offers governed publishing; but remote_mcp tools allow plaintext Authorization headers and skills/MCP sources are overridable per invocation.

facts.claim: 'The harness treats all skill content as trusted input. It does not validate, sanitize, or inspect the content or source of skills'; skills can be overridden per call.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D06.rationale: Harness skills (markdown + scripts) are fetched from S3/Git at invocation and treated as trusted input with no validation; callers can override the skills field per InvokeHarness.

facts.claim: Per-user credential scoping (Token Vault, OBO exchange) only available with Bearer JWT inbound auth, not SigV4.
facts.label: from-official-docs

facts.claim: GHSA-hqf8-7w95-9r33 / CVE-2026-15737: sensitive content disclosure via OpenTelemetry spans in bedrock-agentcore-sdk-python (1.4.8, 1.5.0), fixed >=1.5.1 (published 2026-07-16).
facts.label: from-official-docs
facts.relabelled: A09: source/API read, not a local test

D07.rationale: AgentCore Identity Token Vault stores OAuth/API-key credentials, execution roles use IAM; limitations: SigV4 callers lose per-user credential scoping; plaintext MCP headers possible; CVE-2026-15737 leaked sensitive content into OTel spans in the SDK.

D08.rationale: N/A (managed runtime); Step Functions InvokeHarness integration exists.

facts.claim: Memory events are scoped by actorId + sessionId; omitting memory config in the service API provisions managed memory, CLI harnesses default to memory disabled.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D09.rationale: AgentCore Memory: events scoped by actorId+sessionId, configurable strategies and eventExpiryDuration; service API provisions managed memory by default whereas CLI-created harnesses default to memory disabled.

facts.claim: Harness does not validate additionalParams, apiBase, modelId; callers able to set them can redirect requests, override headers (incl. Authorization) or attempt role assumption.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D10.rationale: Per-session microVMs; AWS shared-responsibility note: any principal passing IAM/JWT gate reaches the full session and its tools; customers must validate model additionalParams/apiBase/modelId and skills overrides.

facts.claim: Every harness action is traced automatically through AgentCore Observability; policy enforcement decisions are logged through CloudWatch.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D11.rationale: All actions traced to CloudWatch/X-Ray via AgentCore Observability; Policy decisions logged to CloudWatch; CloudTrail logging for Code Interpreter.

facts.claim: 'AgentCore may use and store your content to improve your service experience or performance. Such improvements would be for your use of AgentCore and not for other customers.'
facts.label: from-official-docs

D12.rationale: AgentCore docs state it 'may use and store your content to improve your service experience or performance' (for the customer's use only); retention beyond memory expiry not verified.

facts.claim: Harness managed container image is pulled from ECR Public on public network and from a private ECR repo harness-<region> in VPC mode.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D13.rationale: SDK and starter toolkit are Apache-2.0 on GitHub with GHSA/CVE history; harness managed image pulled from ECR Public (public mode) or private ECR (VPC mode).

facts.claim: InvokeHarness requires both bedrock-agentcore:InvokeHarness and bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntime on the harness ARN.
facts.label: from-official-docs

D14.rationale: IAM on harness and underlying runtime ARNs, execution roles, resource policies, VPC, JWT authorizers and Policy engines give strong central controls; enforcement of an organisation-wide default is up to the customer.

facts.claim: bedrock-agentcore-sdk-python CVEs: CVE-2026-12530, CVE-2026-16796 (install_packages argument injection), CVE-2026-15737; starter toolkit CVE-2026-4269, CVE-2026-105812, CVE-2026-106032.
facts.label: from-official-docs
facts.relabelled: A09: source/API read, not a local test

D15.rationale: AWS issues GHSA+CVE for AgentCore SDK and starter toolkit (6 CVEs across 2026); bug bounty not verified; the Code Interpreter DNS finding received no CVE.
